utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. My apologies that we're a little late coming in. Ms. Gopalan, you have a matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I have a short procedural application to make, Your Honours, before the next witness is called in. It's an oral application to add an exhibit to our exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The exhibit is 65 ter 05339, and this exhibit has five colour photographs that were provided by the next witness Madam Shyhrete Dula to the OTP during the proofing session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: My client just told me that he can't get the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be dealt with. Carry on, please, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So these were photographs that were provided by Madam Dula during the proofing session in July, and these five photographs are part of a total of 11 photographs that she provided to us. These 11 photographs have been disclosed to the Defence as 65 ter exhibits the following day after we received them, that was the 9th of July, and the Defence was also provided information about these photographs in the supplemental information sheet that we circulated to the Defence. The Prosecution has selected five of the most useful photographs from these 11, and these are the five photographs that are contained in the exhibit that we would like to add to the exhibit list, Your Honours. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is the subject matter of the photographs directly the subject of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The subject matter of the photographs relate to matters directly addressed in the witness's statement and matters raised in the indictment, and I would also submit that all parties and the Chamber will benefit from such photographs, colour photographs, that relate to matters arising in the witness's testimony. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic. Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We agree that we did receive them on 8 July -- I believe 9 July, 2009, and they were included in the proofing note, and we do believe that they are relevant, actually, to her testimony; however, we would like to note our objection that we would have liked to have received them much earlier. In the proofing note she states that she showed them to the Office of the Prosecutor when giving her statement in 2001, and they were not taken then or they were not dealt with then. Furthermore, we would have liked an application for addition to the 65 ter list in advance of today, preferably when they would have used them in the supplemental information sheet. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be added to the 65 ter list, Ms. Gopalan, but you will feel the gentle sting in the tail of the submissions of Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Duly noted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's clearly been a failure of courtesy at the very least.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Duly noted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Ms. Gopalan has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Dula.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Please could you state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I am Shyhrete Dula.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What is your date of birth, Madam Dula?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I was born on the 21st of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: In what year?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Dula, where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I live in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal in September 2001?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And have you recently had the opportunity to review this statement?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, having reviewed the statement, Madam, I understand that you wished to make a number of corrections to the statement.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I will read out these corrections for your confirmation.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The statement is 65 ter 05162.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And the first correction refers to the English page 2, second paragraph, it's the same reference for the B/C/S, and it relates to the houses in your family compound. At present the paragraph reads: "The second house which is slightly smaller than mine housed my sister and brother-in-law together with their two children. The third and smallest house was that of my mother-in-law." I will now read out the correction that you wish to make: "The second house which is slightly smaller than mine housed my mother-in-law, sister-in-law, and brother-in-law together with his two children. The third and smallest house belonged to my mother-in-law and was the summer house." Is that the correction that you wish to make?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move on to the second correction that you wished to make and this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, did you mean the correction to be that it housed by mother-in-law, sister-in-law, and brother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Perhaps I could rephrase the correction, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Maybe the witness could tell us.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam, could you tell us who lived in the second house, the house that was slightly smaller than yours?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: In the second house it was my brother-in-law, his wife, and my mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. I'd now like to move on to the English page 2, last sentence, and the B/C/S page 2, second-last paragraph, last sentence. At present the paragraph reads: "I heard the distinctive crack of flames, and at about 1.30 on the 25th of March our compound gate suddenly flew open, having been struck by what I subsequently recognised to be a police jeep." Madam, during the proofing session you clarified that you did not see the compound gate flying open and that it was your mother-in-law who saw this and told you about the police jeep. Is that the correction that you wish to make to this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving on to the final few corrections, and this is in English page 3, the fourth paragraph, the last sentence; and the B/C/S page 3, third paragraph, last sentence. The last sentence reads: "I could not make out much of what was being said, but I heard much cursing." This is in relation to when you sought refuge in the house of the stranger in Rruga e Mullirit, Gjakove. Am I correct that the correction you wish to make to this paragraph is that this sentence should be deleted from this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I said that I heard the cursing when I was in my own house, when they entered the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. So you had heard the cursing earlier on?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And this takes us to the next correction that you wish to make to your statement, and this is when you were in your house. And you said - and this is in English, page 3, the second-last sentence; and B/C/S, page 2, the last paragraph, second sentence which reads: "I believe that their accents were those of Serbs from Gjakove ..." After this sentence you wished to add the sentence that we have just deleted which was: "I could not make out much of what was being said, but I heard much cursing." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally let's go to the English page 4, third-last paragraph, the second sentence; and the B/C/S page 4, second paragraph. This correction is made in relation to the crowd you saw being escorted out of Gjakove. The sentence at the moment reads: "They were escorted by a mixture of VJ soldiers and Serbian police and, we assumed, were being led out of Gjakove." Madam, what was the correction you wished to make to this sentence in relation to the crowd that was being escorted out by the VJ soldiers and Serbian police?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: My correction would be that when we left our homes and we were directed towards Albania, we were escorted by policemen. Up to the border we were escorted, initially by police and then by soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. And now, having made these corrections to your statement, are you satisfied that its contents are true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Everything I stated is true. I experienced everything during the first night of NATO attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender the statement into evidence. It's 65 ter 05160.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01268.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd now like to read out the witness's in-court summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The witness is from the town of Djakovica or Gjakove in the Djakovica municipality. She will testify that on the night of the 24th to 25th March, 1999, forces of the FRY and Serbia expelled Kosovo Albanian residents from their homes. The witness's house was situated in the centre of the Mahala e Hadumit area of Djakovica, a historic quarter comprising an old shopping bazaar and a mosque. She will testify that, during the night of the 24th of March, 1999, and the early hours of the 25th of March, 1999, she heard Serbian voices outside her street. Later that night, policemen entered the yard of her family compound and started shooting. The witness and her family managed to escape and sought refuge in a nearby house. She could see her house and all the surrounding buildings burning from there. She will describe the destruction in her neighbourhood, the bazaar shops and buildings burning, and the old mosque and minaret damaged. She will testify that her house and her mother-in-law's house were burned down and that she found her brother-in-law dead in his house. She will describe how on the morning of the 25th she and her family sought refuge, along with many others, in a temple where they remained for eight days. On the eighth day, the witness and her family joined a convoy of people heading out of Gjakove. They were escorted out by VJ and policemen to the Qafa e Prushit border crossing. The witness and her family crossed into Albania and were eventually taken to Austria as refugees, where they stayed for six months. The witness says that she left Kosovo because of the actions of the Serbian police. End of in-court summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Dula, as you know, the Judges have your statement before them and therefore I have some clarificatory questions on your statement. Let's begin with the neighbourhood that you lived in. In your statement, Madam, that's the English and B/C/S, page 2, paragraph 1, you say that your home was situated in the Mahala e Hadumit area of Gjakove and that this area was a shopping bazaar and built in Turkish style and there was a mosque, a very old mosque, in the area as well. Now, Madam, these shops in the shopping bazaar, could you tell us what sorts of shops they were, in other words what did they sell?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: These shops traded privately various kinds of goods, and they also exercised artisan crafts work there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And for how long had these artisans or craft works been exercised in these shops, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: You mean before the war?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They continued to work until one day before the war, but they used to close very early during the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us what crafts they -- these artisans made in these shops if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: There were people who made the traditional hats of the Albanian costumes, folk costumes, various boutiques.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Now these people who made the traditional hats of the Albanian costumes, could you tell us for how long they had been making these hats in the bazaar, since when if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I'm not sure for how long but it was a years'-long tradition.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Now, moving on to the events on the 24th of March, 1999, that you talk about in your statement, you say that at approximately midnight on the 24th of March you heard a commotion in the street outside your compound. This is in the English page 2, paragraph 4; the B/C/S page 2, last paragraph. But just to clarify, this street in which you heard the commotion outside your house, is this the street with the shopping bazaars that we just spoke about?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And you say you also heard voices speaking in Serbian on the street. Madam, do you understand or speak Serbian?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I understand Serbian very well, but I cannot speak it properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. On this day, Madam, at around midnight on the 24th of March, who else was with you in your home?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: As usual, the whole family: myself, my husband, and my three children.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. What about those in the family compound that you spoke about, who else was present in the family compound?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: In the family compound that included my home you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: In my mother-in-law's house there was my mother-in-law; her son; my brother-in-law; his wife; and their children, their two children.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, moving on to the English page 2, paragraph 4; and that's the B/C/S page 2, second-last paragraph, you say: "At this stage we stayed in our houses where I woke up the children and waited, hoping that the voices would go away; however, I soon became aware of the sound of wood burning outside in the bazaar. I heard the distinctive crack of flames ..." Now, when you say you heard the sound of wood burning, did you subsequently discover what it is that was burning, what it is that you heard burning?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Next to my house, a little bit beyond, there are all the shops in the bazaar and they were all burning at the time that I heard that noise that you read about.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that at this stage some 30 people entered your yard. They were firing automatic weapons as they advanced. This is in the English page 3, paragraph 2; and the B/C/S page 2, the last paragraph onwards. Now, as these 30 people entered your yard, Madam, did they say anything?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: As soon as they entered the yard they began cursing and shouting.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us what it is they were shouting about?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They were very -- they were things that I cannot mention here, swear words.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And did they ask you and your family to do anything?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: We did not have any contact with them because we jumped over the wall.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you describe to us what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They were wearing police uniforms, blue camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you say that you jumped over the wall. Could you tell us from which part of the house is it that you escaped?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: We escaped from the back part of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And who was with you as you were escaping, who else were you escaping with?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: My children, myself, and my husband.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And as you were escaping, did you fear for the safety of any particular member of your family?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. I knew that my mother-in-law, my brother-in-law, and his family, they were all inside in their own house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: How about the immediate members of your family who you were fleeing with, escaping from your house with, within your immediate members of your family? Did you fear the safety of any particular one of them?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes. For as long as I was inside the house, I was very scared because I had heard that they had committed major crimes, they had raped young girls and women and they had killed people.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how had you heard this, Madam Dula?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: People were speaking about that. When we spoke to other people we heard those things.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you say that you fled from the wall -- you jumped over the wall and this was at the back part of the house. Could you tell us if you suffered any injuries as a result of fleeing from the back of your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, I suffered major injuries. My face and the whole body was in pain.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did anyone else in your family suffer any injuries?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, my husband too. He injured his leg.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. I'd now like to move on to when you sought refuge in the house of a strange in the Rruga e Mullirit area of Gjakove. So this is after you fled your family home. This is in the English page 3, paragraph 4; and the B/C/S page 3, paragraph 3. Now, Madam, when you were in the house of the stranger, could you tell us what it is you saw from the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: While I was in the house of the stranger I was able to observe in the direction of my house, and I could see that it was entirely burned, it was all in flames.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: In addition to your house being in flames, could you see anything else in the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, the shops were also in flames.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, you say that on the morning of the 25th of March, 1999, you made your way back to your house - this is in English page 3, the last paragraph; B/C/S page 3, the third-last paragraph - you say that as you were making your way back to your house, you were shocked to see the level of destruction that had taken place in your neighbourhood. Madam, could you describe the condition of your neighbourhood to us?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The whole neighbourhood was levelled to the ground. Everything that once stood in this neighbourhood was burned down.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Earlier on you mentioned a mosque in your neighbourhood. First could you tell us the name of this mosque?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It was called the Hadum mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what if anything did you notice in relation to the Hadum mosque?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: When I passed by, I noticed that the minaret was also damaged, it was destroyed in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. In addition to the minaret being damaged, did you notice anything else about the condition of the Hadum mosque?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I saw the minaret. I noticed some damages on the other side of the mosque too, but I didn't dare look and inspect the damages further.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Were you able to observe what it is that caused these damages that you saw on the other side of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I saw that the walls of the mosque, the external walls, were damaged, and I continued.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd now like to call up 65 ter 05351.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam, shortly a photograph will appear on the screen before you. I'm afraid it's not very clear, but are you able to recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This photograph depicts part of the street where I live.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Are you able to observe anything specific in relation to this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The street where my house is here in this part, here we can see the shops of the old bazaar.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And where is your house in relation to these shops?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: In this part here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If you could just draw an arrow indicating the direction of your house.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Am I correct that your house is located where you have just placed the marking on the photograph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, in that part of the street that we see.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That is where your house is located?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do we know when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam, are you able to tell us when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This photograph was most probably taken when the war started, immediately after the attack, after these shops were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Why do you say that, Madam?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: You can see still on the photograph the smoke, at least I can see that on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Where is it you see the photograph -- apologies, the smoke in the photograph, Madam?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Here, this part here. I think there's smoke there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Are you able to place a letter A to where you see the smoke?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Here and here too. May I mark this too?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this exhibit that the witness has just marked has already been tendered into evidence and we do have information as to when the photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. You want this now exhibited?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the marked photograph will be Exhibit P01269.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you know the exhibit number of the photograph, the existing exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours, it's P1105. And this photograph is an enlargement of the lower of the two photographs contained in that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd now like to call up another exhibit, that's P1104. Could we please go to the second page of this exhibit to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes. This also shows that part of the street where my house is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And when was the street in this condition?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: After the war. It was rebuilt.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So this is a photograph of the rebuilt street that you lived on?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd now like to go to the first page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, Madam?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes. This is the part behind the mosque, the rear part.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: How about the buildings just in front of the mosque, do you know what they are?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: These buildings were shops.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: When was it you saw -- or did you see these shops and the mosque in this condition?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: When we were expelled and directed towards Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Am I correct that you passed these buildings on your way out towards Albania?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us approximately when that was?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact time of the day, but as far as I remember it was the 2nd of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Now, just before we leave this photograph, if we have a look at the mosque there is a tall structure to the right of the mosque. Could you tell us what that is and what has happened to that structure?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This is the minaret of the mosque and the top part of the minaret was damaged; it collapsed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when did you see the minaret in that condition having collapsed?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The following day when I went to look for my mother-in-law and also on that day when we left for Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd now like to call up another exhibit, that's P1107.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, Madam?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the front part of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when was it you saw the mosque in this condition?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The day we left for Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. I'd now like to ask you some questions about the condition of your own home when you returned to your family compound on the morning of the 25th of March. Now, this is in the English page 4, paragraph 2; and the B/C/S page 3, the second-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: In the meanwhile could we call up 65 ter 05339, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam, when you returned to your home on the 25th of March, 1999, could you tell us what condition your house was in on that day?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The following day when I went to my house, I saw a complete ruin. I could not even enter it because of the ruins.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And could you tell us what it is that had ruined your house, what had caused the damage to your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Only the policemen that night could have caused that ruin.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Were you able to observe yourself any marks or indications of what had caused the damage to your home?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I wasn't able to observe that because I only went there to look for my mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the condition of your mother-in-law's house was?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The old house where she used to live was in a more or less good state, whereas the auxiliary building was burnt to the ground like my own house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, Madam, on the screen before you there is a photograph. Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes. This is the entrance. The police broke down this gate and entered our yard. This is the entrance to the yard of my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And could you tell us who took this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: After the war, before we started to clean up all this mess, we took a photograph of the gate.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: When did you observe your house in this condition; in other words, when was the first time you saw your house in this condition?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The next day, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page, please, of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, Madam?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the house where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: From which angle is this photograph taken of the house that you live in?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It was taken from the entrance to the yard, from that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when did you observe the house in this condition?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The following day, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how did your house look prior to the events of the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It resembled a normal house, like all other houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: We can observe from this photograph that the roof of the house seems to be missing. Do you know what happened to the top floor of the house? Were you able to observe any causes of the damage?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The top part was in flames, the first and the second floor as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could we move on to the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What does this photograph show, Madam, if you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: These are photographs of the rooms. You can see here part of the kitchen. It depicts the damage they caused inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, towards the right side of the photograph there is some dark colours visible to the right side of the photograph. Are you able to tell us what caused those dark markings on the walls?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They were all caused by the fire, the flames they caused.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And can we move on to the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What about this photograph, Madam, what does this show?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the first floor of my house, where I was staying that night. We had to pass through here to get to the kitchen and jump through the window to the other courtyards.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, the condition that this room is in now, when did you observe the room to be in this condition?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, these last three photographs that we have seen, who took these photographs -- or the last four photographs that we have seen, who took these photographs?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: My children, they took these photographs after we returned home.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender the first four pages of this exhibit into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01270.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, moving on to another area, Madam, when you were expelled from your home the night before you returned to see your house in this condition, did your brother-in-law leave with your family?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, he didn't leave with us. He was in his own house. We were in our own house. Both houses are in the same yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did he leave at all that night?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us what happened to your brother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The next day in the morning when I went back I saw him dead. It was a horrible scene for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did you learn what had happened to him, how he had been killed?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I saw his body with my own eyes. It was completely massacred.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you know why it is that your brother-in-law didn't leave his house that night?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: My house was situated in a different part, more convenient part, and had his house been situated in a more convenient part he would have survived too.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us his name, please?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Kujtim.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could we have his full name, please.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Kujtim Dula.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how old was he then?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could I call up 65 ter 05339 again, please, and go to the last page of the exhibit, page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, while the exhibit is coming up, Madam Dula, do you know of any other relatives of yours who were killed during this time in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: In my family there are two persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you know their names?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Astrit Rexha.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when was Astrit Rexha killed, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Astrit was killed when he was forced to join the convoy to Albania, when the people were expelled from their homes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: When was that, Madam Dula?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the date, but I learnt from his mother about his death.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And did you also learn who it was who was responsible for his death?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The policemen who expelled them from their house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Were any other members of your family killed at this time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The son of my mother-in-law's sister was also killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what was his name?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Agim Haxhi Avdy li.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us where he was killed and when, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I don't know about the date, but I learnt from his mother that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how was he killed?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know any details about this person. I only learned that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Now, the photograph before you, could you tell us what it depicts, please, if you know.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The crime committed on my now late brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And who took this photograph, Madam?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: My son.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when was this taken?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The next day. He found a small camera that belonged to the family and took this picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this photograph into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01271.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, Madam, I'd like to move on to when you left Gjakove - and this is in the English page 4, paragraph 3; and the B/C/S page 4, the second paragraph. This was in the -- on the eighth day that you were in the temple and you say you saw a crowd of people walking past the temple from the direction of the Qerim district of Gjakove and that your family decided to join the crowd and leave Gjakove. Could you tell us who escorted you out of Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Along the way there were two check-points manned by policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Where were these check-points, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The first check-point was at the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you know the name of this bridge, Madam?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: As far as I know it is called the bridge of Mete Efendi.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that these two check-points were manned by policemen. How did you know that they were policemen?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Because they were wearing police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what do you understand to be the police uniform?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They were blue camouflage uniforms, and as far as I know they are police colours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned two check-points. Where was the second check-point located? You've already mentioned the bridge as the first one.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The second check-point was located near the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before you reached the check-points when you were still in the town of Gjakove, could you tell us who escorted you out of the town then?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And while they were escorting you out of town, did you see them do anything?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Up to the first check-point, we could see policemen causing damage to the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you explain to us what you mean by "causing damage to the buildings"? For example, which buildings? What were they doing to the building?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The shops, the grocery shops that were along the side of the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what were they doing to the grocery shops?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They were breaking the window-panes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And after breaking the window-panes did they do anything else?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They went inside, but we continued our way so I did not see what they did after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. And now a question about your identity card. You say that when you joined the convoy in Gjakove, you were asked to hand over -- you and your family were asked to hand over your identity cards. Could you tell us on how many occasions on your trip out of Gjakove were you asked for your identity cards?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: We were asked for our identity cards at the first check-point and also the second check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And who asked for your identity cards at both these check-points?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Policemen, the ones that were manning those points.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what happened after they asked you for your identity cards? What did they do to them, if anything?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I did not have anything to give to them because everything had been burned, everything that my family had had been burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you were part of a convoy. Were other members of the convoy also asked for their identity cards at these check-points?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes. All of their identity cards were taken away from them and they were put in two big boxes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If you know, Madam, approximately how many others were in the convoy with you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number; however, it was an endless convoy. That's what I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And could you tell us where it is that you crossed into Albania?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: At Qafa e Prushit, in the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And at this stage, who was escorting you out of Albania [sic]?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The army.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Now, finally could you tell us why it is that you and your family left Kosovo at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The reason we left Kosovo was to live, to survive. There was no other way for us to live than to escape.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And who were you escaping from, Madam?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: We were escaping from the policemen. They expelled us.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage I have no further questions for this witness and I thank you for your indulgence in allowing me to go over my allocated time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Good morning, ma'am. My name is Marie O'Leary. I'm here representing Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic today in these proceedings. With me is our lead counsel, Mr. Dragoljub Djordjevic. We have your statement in evidence, but I just want to make sure that we go through a couple of points just to make sure that we have everything clarified for the record. And as is procedure with these statements, my understanding is that it was given orally in Albanian; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And then it was prepared in English and read back to you for you to confirm and sign; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And that's -- you don't speak any English; is that correct, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you said today you understand some Serbian; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And I just want to orient ourselves to where things happened in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So if we could have the map at P823, page 29, called up.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you lived in Gjakove your entire life; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so you went to school in Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And what was the last year of school you had finished?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I had eight years of schooling. I got married very young.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I'm afraid we don't have the right map. One moment. It's on page 29. Oh, great, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, here's a pretty rudimentary map of Gjakove, and I just want to kind of figure out where some of these neighbourhoods are that you've been discussing. Some of them are listed to some degree quite lightly on the map, if you can see them there. Can you see them on the screen? Can you see where the area of Mahala e Hadumit is on this map, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I can't read these letters very well. I can see Mahala e Haxhiymerit but not Mahala e Hadumit.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, without reading it, ma'am, can you just see -- can you tell by the way the roads are oriented here, since you lived there your whole life; can you tell from that map where that area should be?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This part here is the centre of town; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Could you circle what you think is the centre of town, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This one here.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. So if that's the centre of town, can you tell me approximately where Mahala e Hadumit is.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Mahala e Hadumit must be in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Could you make an indication on the screen of a number 1?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: From the street lights you go south and this is where Mahala e Hadumit should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. And I see a little red mark on there. Could you make that 1 a little bit bigger where you made that mark, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me, then, where Rruga e Mullirit is on this map.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Well, it is Rruga e Qabrat but part of it is called Rruga e Mullirit. It is right next to Mahala e Hadumit.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Right next to it in which direction, to the right or to the left or above it or below it?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: To the right, as you go towards my house. There's a small pathway from my house and then you get to this street.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And approximately where would your house be on this map, ma'am, if you can tell?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I find it difficult to orientate myself in this map; however, I'll try. From the centre you have to go this way to get to my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, I can't quite see what you've marked on there. Can you draw a little bit darker, approximately where you think your house would be.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: As I said, from the centre you take the road and it should be here.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So just a little bit farther underneath what you've already marked; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And is the home that you're staying in on the evening of the 24th and the 25th, is that in the same area there?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, in -- on Qabrati road or street, that's where it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And later on you discussed the big temple that you took shelter in. Is that also located in these areas or is it further out anywhere on the map?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It is on the opposite part from where I live. You have to go through an alley-way and then get to that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I would tender this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00352.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You stated that your house at the time was in a family compound surrounded by a high wall. Can you tell me approximately how high these walls were?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It must have been about 2 metres high.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And approximately how thick were the walls?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Well, the normal thickness of all surrounding walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Would you be able to tell me in centimetres?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: 20 centimetres, the thickness of a brick I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And they circled the entire perimeter of the compound?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. Ma'am, I'd like to call up a blank piece of paper actually at D004-3445.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If it's not in the e-court system yet, then alternatively a blank screen should suffice.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, I was wondering if you could just draw a couple of things in a quick diagram that would help us understand the relation of all the buildings in your compound so we can better understand that evening. If you could start off and draw a large square that would indicate the walls of the compound. You can draw right on the screen that's in front of you. And actually --

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I was thinking of actually a little bit larger because that will be the walls and we'll draw the houses within it.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So if we could just clear the screen and redo it one more time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And just draw a very large square, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you put a G where the gate would be in your compound.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This is the surrounding wall. You said what letter? G?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: G where the gate is.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. Are there any other entrances or exits or is it just the one gate?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This is the only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And approximately how wide was that gate?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The gate was approximately 2 metres. I'm only speaking approximately. I can't give you the exact length or height.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. If you could draw three smaller boxes inside that box that would indicate the three homes that are in the compound: the three buildings, your home, your mother-in-law's home, and the summer house I believe you referred to it as.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: My brother-in-law's house was here, my house was here, and the summer house was here.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Can you mark your home with a number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And your brother-in-law's house with a number 2.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And the summer house with a 3, please.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so by this diagram, your house was closest to the gate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And approximately how far is it from your house -- the edge of your house, to the gate?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: About 10 metres, maybe less.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And the main street is directly outside that gate; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And do you know approximately how many square metres the whole entirety of the yard would be within the walls?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It's about 5 acres [as interpreted], I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And are there any other buildings within those walls?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No. The old house was a historical building. It was a 200-years'-old house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Which house was that, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The one where my brother-in-law lived and my mother-in-law as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: The one at number 2; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. That helped me orient myself on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If I could tender this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must have a break now, and we'll resume at 11.00, and a Court Officer will assist you during the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down. Yes, Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ms. Dula, when we left we were talking about your compound and we were discussing the layout. The gate on the door, you said in your statement, afforded you full privacy from the road. So you couldn't see the road from your compound, from within the compound; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And on the evening of March 24th and going into the morning of March 25th, you said you heard a commotion out in the streets around midnight that caught your attention?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you said specifically it was voices and that caught your attention because it would be unusual for people to gather in the street late at night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So is it safe to say that it was quiet entirely up until midnight?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you were in your home with your family at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And, ma'am, how old were your children at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: My daughter was 18; my son was younger, 16 and a half; and the youngest was about 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And at that time your sister, is it, was with her -- with your brother-in-law, your mother-in-law, and their children in the house that was marked number 2; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, my mother-in-law, my sister-in-law, my brother-in-law, and their two children.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, just to clarify your familial relationships, is this your sister or your sister-in-law?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It's my sister-in-law, not my sister.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Are these relatives of your husband then?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: My husband's brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So your mother-in-law, then, you're referring to your husband's mother; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And how old were their two children at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: One was 3; and the other, 2 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And at the time you heard these voices speaking outside the wall then, you said they were speaking Serbian and that because of the NATO action you became quickly concerned. Could you hear what the voices were saying, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: While they were out in the street, I couldn't make anything of their voices; when they entered our courtyard, I could hear them cursing.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And at this time you heard the voices you would have been inside your house, they would have been outside the wall, and there was approximately 10 metres' distance between, at least, as you said; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you could distinguish that it was Serbian they were speaking; yes?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So they were speaking pretty loud?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Would you say they were shouting?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They were talking among themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And at some point your husband was concerned and went out to barricade the door then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The gate was locked and my husband was not able to go outside. Maybe this was a mistake in my statement that I wish to correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Perhaps, ma'am. On page 2 in the English version of your statement - and your statement is P1268, if we want to call it up, I'm not sure which page in Albanian, possibly 2, potentially on page 3 - but I'll read you the sentence I'm referring to. You say: "Because of the NATO action that night, I quickly became concerned. My husband went into the yard and placed wood against our gate which opens inward as a makeshift barricade." Are you saying now that that didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I'm not changing my statement. I already stated that when the NATO attack started the gate to the yard was locked. My husband went from the room to the corridor when he heard the commotion, when he saw that the yard was getting filled with policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, what time did the NATO attacks start that evening?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: To my recollection it was sometime after 8.00 p.m. I don't know if this is the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you're referring to the 24th of March that evening, at 8.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And when you say the NATO attacks started, do you mean that there were air-strikes on Djakovica at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So when you were saying that it was quiet up until midnight you didn't refer to the NATO air-strikes, you simply meant that there were no voices in the street; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Because from 8.00 on there was obviously some air noise, perhaps explosions going on?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: There were some air noise and we went inside the house. There was no need for us to remain outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so from 8.00 on that night you were all inside the house and nobody left?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So nobody went out to make a barricade for the door; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, nobody went out. As I said, the gate was locked, as we usually lock it during the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay, ma'am. The reason I ask about that is because when you speak about him making this barricade it's after you hear the voices, after midnight, in your statement. So you're saying that he made this barricade earlier in the evening and that basically he locked the gate earlier in the evening. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I stated what I already told you several times now. I made a correction to this part of my statement. There was probably misinterpretation or it was erroneously translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, ma'am. Did you ever then during the night speak with your brother-in-law's family?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No. They were in their own house; we were in our house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And at some point in the night you said you heard the sound of wood burning outside the bazaar and the distinctive crack of flames; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And in your statement that comes after midnight, approximately 1.30 I believe it is; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Approximately. I don't know exactly what time it was. We were going through difficult times then.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. In your statement you don't note seeing the fire or smelling any fire. Did you see or smell any fire at this time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: While I was in my own house I wasn't able to see or smell any fire because you cannot see anything from my house. But when we left to this other house, it's then when I was able to see the flames.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. Moving on to the third page of your statement you say: "Around 1.30 the compound gate flew open having been struck with what I subsequently recognised to be a police jeep." But you've now corrected this today for us and said that you didn't actually see this, did you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I didn't see anything myself when they entered the yard, but my mother-in-law, whose house was just opposite the gate, could see it. She's 90 years old now.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So at the time she was about 80 years old; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, 81.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And she was in your brother-in-law's house when she saw this; yes?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And be -- you placed that house further from the gate, we could say that it's more than 10 metres away then, at least; correct? Do you have any estimate of how far your brother's house is from the gate -- your brother-in-law's house, excuse me, from the gate?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: From my house the gate is about 10 metres away; his house is a little bit further away, I would say about 15 metres from the gate.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And when did she tell you she had seen this?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The following day when we met.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And what did she tell you exactly that she saw?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: She told me how they were taken outside the house, how they detained her son. She wanted to remain with her son, but she was made to go outside with her daughter-in-law and the two children.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, I don't have any of that in your statement, so we'll get to that actually as far as what happened later that evening. But I just want to discuss the police jeep that she said she saw right now. So if you could tell me what she said exactly happened when she said a police jeep crashed through the gates.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They entered like madmen, she said. They were firing on all sides of the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How did your mother know this was a police jeep? Did she tell you or did she just say "police"?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Most probably she knew it was a police car because we saw police cars on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So when she told you the story about the gate being crashed in, she used the words "police jeep"; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: She didn't actually describe the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so then you go on to describe the 30 people that had entered into your yard firing automatic weapons in no particular direction as they advanced. You actually saw this part, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't. It was my mother-in-law who told me this. She said there were about 30 of them who entered the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you see anything in your yard that evening, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes. I only saw this red light on the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You saw a red light in the yard, but you didn't see any of the individuals, did you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I did see individuals as they climbed that part of the balcony which is near to the entrance to the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So a second ago you said you didn't see the 30 people enter into the yard firing automatic weapons. So the first time you saw them is when they were coming on to your balcony of your house, on the front steps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes. The entrance door to the corridor is made of glass and you could see them. As I was leaving, I could see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So am I correct to understand that you saw the men coming up to your door-step -- to your front steps, and at that point it's when you left out the back window; is that correct, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And the glass in your door, is it transparent or is it opaque?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, it's transparent. I could see them but they could not see me.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was there any curtain in the window, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And was it pulled shut at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, they were pulled shut.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was there a curtain on this transparent glass door?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you talk about a red light and you say that everything was in this red light but you don't know the source of it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The light was coming from the gate, from the entrance to the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And it was dark outside at this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so the only lighting was this red lighting; yes?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so you saw these men coming up your steps very briefly; that's correct, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you note they were wearing -- in your statement you say "blue camouflage uniform of the Serbian police," and you say you're positive of this?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What made you so positive?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: As I said, through the glass of the entrance door to the corridor I saw one of them dressed in that uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So of the people you saw, you saw one man in a blue camouflage uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I only saw that one which was nearer to the door, as I was trying to flee.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you say it was definitely not the uniform of soldiers in your statement, why not?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I didn't see any military uniform there.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Can you describe what you mean by a military uniform that you would expect to see?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: A military uniform is greyish.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Is it solid colour?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, the military one.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you see -- in that brief moment that you saw this one person, did you see any sort of insignia or armband?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, it was impossible to notice any insignia because, as I said, I happened to see him through the glass door as I was trying to leave the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So the only lighting you would have had to see this man who was coming up your steps was in a red light; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that red light can change the colour that you see?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Certainly. Would you agree with me that if you have a red light shining on an object it can change the way you see the colour of the object; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I believe it cannot change the way you see the colour because through light you can see the object.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you don't believe that the red light affected the colour you saw?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The blue colour can be distinguished under any other colour light.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you don't believe with me that a blue colour under a red light might actually appear black?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Not black. You can still tell it's blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And at this time did you hear any voices speaking Albanian, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you hear any other languages other than Serbian?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Only Serbian. I could hear them swear in my own yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so at this point you and your family went out the back window; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And by your accounts there are 30 police officers entering the yard according to your mother-in-law at this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You made the statement that the police officers did not give chase; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you didn't speak to any of these people she defined as police officers; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was it possible these people that you saw in camouflage were actually doing evacuations related to fire and/or missiles?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was it possible that they're not police, that they're actually paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was it possible they were VJ?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, not soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Because of the uniform?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, because of the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was it possible they were UCK?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Why is that, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
