utterances.text: It hadn't happened before. We never heard of such a case.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you've stated today you had no contact with them, so you can't be certain who they were exactly, can you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Well, you can understand who they are because of their accent. When they speak then you can see who they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you don't know what they wanted either, do you, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: That was all happening very suddenly. We did not expect that to happen. My children were asleep as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You say your children were asleep at the time that you went out the window?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, but I woke them up previously, before we heard the commotion.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: The timing of that in your statement is a little bit different actually, because you're talking in your statement - and again we're on page 2 of the English, page 2 of the Albanian, if you want to look at the bottom - where you discuss that at approximately midnight you heard this commotion in the street. And you go on to say it would be unusual and everyone was in their respective homes. And you said: "By listening closer I established that the voices were that ... speaking Serbian and, because of the NATO action that night, I quickly became concerned." This is where you said: "My husband went into the yard and placed wood against our gate, which opens inwards, as a makeshift barricade. We stayed in our houses, where I woke my children ... hoping the voices would go away."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel read slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I apologise, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: "Placed a piece of wood" - is where we're at here - "against our gate, which opens inwards," and -- "as a makeshift barricade. We stayed in our houses, where I woke my children, and waited, hoping the voices would go away." So did you wake your children before you heard the voices or after, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: As soon as I heard the commotion in the street and the voices, I woke my children up. I also told the other people I spoke to during the proofing that this needs to be corrected. I did not say that my husband went to put wood against the gate as it is in the statement. I corrected it.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Are you saying you made other changes to your statement in proofing that weren't reflected here today, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: There were some mistakes, things that I had not said the way they were reflected in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: We went through some of them on direct. Are they all corrected now?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecutor mentioned all the mistakes, and they were corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Except for in this paragraph there were a couple of changes you just made now about the timing of the barricade and waking your children; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And when you went out the back window and you went to, as you describe it, a stranger's house in Rruga e Mullirit - I apologise if I'm mispronouncing the neighbourhood - but how long did it take you to get to this house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: We had to jump about three or four other walls until we got there.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you're saying it's about three or four compounds away?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Why did you decide to stay there, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It was not a decision that we made. We just remained there. We had no force or strength left in us to go any further.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But it doesn't sound like it was that far away from your house. Did you feel safe at this stranger's house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I felt safer there because the part of the town where I lived was all in flames.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Why wouldn't the flames extend to this part, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The flames were on the street. This house was in a different part, on another street.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you know whose house this was, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I know the surname. Their surname was Ymeraga. But I don't know who exactly owned the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you know at the time who was living there?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: We found an old lady there. There was nobody else. We did not get into the house. We stayed in the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you stayed there that evening in the courtyard; is that correct, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And the old lady, was she in the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Initially she stayed inside the house, but then she came to the yard with us, to stay with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Approximately how old was she, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: About 70 or 80 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And you remained in the courtyard the whole evening with your husband and your three children and sometimes this woman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, in your statement on page 3, in the middle, third paragraph in the bottom, you say after you say you sought refuge there that: "From an upper floor at this house I could see my home, together with many of the surrounding buildings, was on fire. As we waited at the stranger's house I could hear voices speaking and shouting in Serbian." Ma'am, if you didn't go into the house, how were you on the upper floor?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, there's -- there are no changes in the statement. We could see from the upper floor what was going on in the other part of town. We just went there for a couple of seconds and then went back to the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So at some point you did go into her home?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, just to see what was going on, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But twice just now you've said you remained in the courtyard the whole evening. You said you never went in the home. Why did you say that you didn't go into the home?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Well, this is not at all different from what I said before. I had also mentioned before that I went to observe what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, just before today at transcript 47, lines 22 and 23, you said: "We found an old lady there. There was nobody else. We did not get into the house. We stayed in the courtyard." But now you're saying you did go into the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: We stayed in the yard the whole time, yes. A little after we went there, I went to see what was going on outside, I went to the upper floor, but then went to the yard again.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So how long were you in the house, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It was about a couple of seconds. I just observed -- was trying to observe what was going on outside and immediately went to the yard again.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did any other of your family members go into the house, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It was just me.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So at some point -- do you know what time it was in the evening that you went into the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It was in the first -- in the early hours of the morning, before dawn I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And dawn at that time would be closer to 6.00, 7.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, earlier than that, 4.00, 4.30. It had not dawned yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this is in March; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So when you went in for a brief second, you went upstairs, you looked out a window, I'm presuming, and what did you see?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I saw my house engulfed in flames.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you see anything else?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The roofs of the house -- the roofs of the shops and the roof of my house were all burning.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So from up there for that second you saw just the roofs of everything burning; is that correct, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And then you went back down into the yard, and I'm assuming that there are walls on this yard too because you said you crawled over three or four walls to get here, so there are walls around this compound as well?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were they approximately 2 metres like yours?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: All surrounding walls are of the same height.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And at that time you said about 4.30 in the morning, before it was light, you say in your statement, so we consider dawn to be after 4.30 that day - I heard what I considered to be shelling, loud explosions coming from the area of your house. My thoughts at that time were that the area was being completely destroyed. So you were in the courtyard when you heard this, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And from the stranger's house you said that you still heard speaking and shouting in Serbian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I did, but it was in my own yard that I heard the exact swear words that they used.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that from the stranger's house you just heard voices; it wasn't as distinct as it was at your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, they weren't, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But it was loud enough you could still hear it was Serbian; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And did you believe that the voices that you were still hearing were the ones coming from your house or were they coming from a different direction, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They were coming from the direction of my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And, ma'am, at 4.30 when you heard these explosions, is it possible that those were NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Because I could hear explosions from the roofs of the shops and houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And what did you imagine those explosions to be?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I think they were caused by the group of policemen that entered our yard. That part of town was destroyed by them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you didn't actually see anybody setting off explosions?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Is it possible the explosions could have been electrical or related to the fires that were ongoing?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Because these houses were set on fire from the inside. The explosions were from the inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How do you know they were from the inside?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: We could see the flames. I could see the flames coming out of our -- out of the windows of my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, to be clear, all you actually saw was burning roofs; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Going back to NATO air-strikes, on page 2 of your statement you say: "I was aware that NATO commenced an air offensive in Serbia, Kosovo, on the night of the 24 of March 1999. My family intended to remain at home in Gjakove, regardless of the NATO air campaign, as we firmly believed that such a campaign would not present any danger to us." Is that accurate, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We were not afraid of NATO attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And when did you first learn about the NATO air-strikes or the potential for NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I heard it on the TV and the news.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were they Serbian stations or Albanian stations, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, most of them were Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But I noticed on the picture of your home that there was a satellite. You were still receiving Albanian television via satellite?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: My children used to watch their programmes. I did not have time to watch TV that much. My children used to watch films and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you were receiving Albanian stations at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And in that statement you gave your family's intention and belief about whether you should leave. Did you have family discussions about whether you should leave due to NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, because we didn't think that we had to leave if NATO would commence their air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you say that in your statement that nobody left because of NATO. How do you know that nobody left?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The people that lived next to me, my neighbourhoods with whom I had contact, I never heard from them say that they were going to leave because of the air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And by this statement you meant that nobody left in advance of March 24th because of the NATO bombings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this is what you've -- the conclusion you came to discussing with your local neighbours; yes?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. They all said that it's not necessary to leave because of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And when you refer to nobody again here, do you mean only Albanians or do you include Serbs, Bosnians, Roma, other ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I did not have any contact with other ethnicities. The people who lived in my neighbourhood, they all said that there was no need for us to leave because of the air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And your entire neighbourhood was Albanian; is that what you're saying, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Are you aware of NATO bombs ever striking Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Not in the part of town where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Where did you hear about them striking?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: At that time we did not have time to ask questions of that sort. We were all stressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: After that time, what did you learn, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Later I heard that they struck their objectives.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What were their objectives, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what their targets were. I was just a simple housewife. I was taking care of my family's day-to-day living and feeding. I did not take part in such discussions.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I understand, but you had said they had struck their objectives, so I just wondered what you meant by that. Do you believe that they ever struck -- there was any collateral damage as a result of these bombings?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No. I did not have the opportunity to hear about such collateral damage. We were stressed. We were distressed, as a matter of fact, at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Of course at the time, ma'am. I was speaking about in the subsequent nine, ten years here what you had heard. Did you ever hear that civilians were killed accidentally by these bombs?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I did not hear anything about such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So I want to talk about the next morning, on the 25th you say that you were very concerned about your mother-in-law so you returned to go get her; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And were you alone or did your whole family go?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Initially I went there myself because I was afraid to take the whole family.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And about what time of morning was it now?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It had already dawned, but I am not able to tell you the exact time now.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. And you state that when you were on your way back did you go the same route -- you didn't actually tell us, but did you go the same route that you went to the stranger's house, over those same three or four walls?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I took another route. It's a shorter route that takes you directly to my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you were out on the street then; yes, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: There are pathways between the surrounding walls of the compounds and you can go through them to get to the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And did you go directly to your compound?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't go there directly. I was trying to see whether there was anybody around, whether I was in any danger or not, and then I moved to my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And what opportunity did you have to see the destruction then at the bazaar, was that on your way into your compound or was that later in the day?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: On the way back to my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And if you were concerned for your mother-in-law, you probably didn't take a long time to assess the damage on the way there then, did you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, I could see the things that had been destroyed on the way to my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you didn't stop-off and look at anything, did you; you went directly to see how your mother-in-law was doing. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, while I was walking I was looking around.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And at that time were some of the buildings still burning?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, that part was still in flames.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was anything being done to put the flames out?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If we could see P1105 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, you state that you were shocked to see the level of destruction that had taken place in your neighbourhood, and we looked at some photographs in your direct exam. I'm going to call one of them up here actually. I believe it was zoomed in on the bottom photo. Ma'am, this was the photo that you earlier today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And is that what it looked like when you were walking home?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you don't know the date of this photograph, do you, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I don't know the date when this photograph was taken; however, I know that this part of town was in flames.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You don't know who took this photograph, do you, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And if we could look at P1270.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And these are some of the pictures that we're going to look at from your house. Ma'am, when you discussed this in direct exam I was trying to figure out what exactly is this a picture of then, is this by the gate?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes. It was caused, this damage, as they broke into the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So those walls that we're looking at, that's the height of the walls, those are the compound walls, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes. This is the street and this is the gate to the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Since you have that pointer there, could you draw in where the gate should be, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This one here.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so is this taken from -- I'm just trying to figure out what these walls are, then, on the outside that extend out. There are walls that came out? Your gate was set in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: These are the walls of the shops on this side. This part of the door was attached or next to the wall of the shop, and this one here is the door to the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Can you circle the walls that adjoined with the shop, please.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This one here joined to the gate, from here to here.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And the shops were to the right and the left or only to the right?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Can we tender this photo, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00354.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 2 of these photographs then.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now, these photographs were taken upon your return from Albania, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And upon your return from Austria; yes?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, upon our return from Austria.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So that's approximately six months later; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So these pictures were now taken in about September of 1999?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: These pictures were taken immediately after the war, when we came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this is a picture of your house, ma'am; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If we could go to page -- picture 3 I guess it would be.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: In this photo, ma'am, you were asked what the damage is on here, all these black markings, and you said that it was related to fire; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And did you just assume that because you had seen your roof on fire?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The whole house was on fire, not only the roof.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, I'm not just asking, ma'am, that you're not qualified in any way to certify fire damage, are you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I'm not qualified in any way to certify that; however, when you see flames coming out of windows you can immediately conclude that these damages have been caused by the fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: That's common sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we look through the window we see another house that's still standing there with a roof and intact. Whose home is that?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It's my neighbour's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was it within your compound?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No. No, no. It's in a different part.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, you said that the walls went all the way around the perimeter, so I'm wondering how we can see that house. Is the wall gone at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. This is taken from the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And if we go to the next photo, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, this is in your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And which floor is this on, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: It's the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And who took these photographs, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: My son.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to discuss a little bit the destruction that you said you saw outside. And you said in your statement that the minaret tower had been snapped and the top was now lying on the ground. And you now today said it was destroyed in fact. How much of the top of the minaret was lying on the ground that morning?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: When I passed by, I was unable to see how much of the top of the minaret was lying on the ground. All I could see was that it was lying on the ground. And I could also see the damages around.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, I'm just wondering how much of the top of the minaret was on the ground. Was it snapped one-third of the way down, half the way down, three-fourths of the way down? How much of the minaret was missing at that point on the 25th of March?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly how much. All I know it was the top part of the minaret.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If we could see P1104, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ma'am, you stated today with that photograph that this is the damage or an accurate rendition of what you would have seen when you were leaving on the 2nd of April; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Is this how it looked on the 25th of March, or were you not able to see it on that day?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I was not able to see everything. I was trying to get there as soon as I could. All I noticed was the top part of the minaret.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. So going back then you enter your compound and you were looking for your mother-in-law. Were you also looking for your sister-in-law and her children?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Who did you find first?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I found them all together with a neighbour, where they had taken shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: At what point did they take shelter?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: That night when they were made to leave the house and when they detained my brother-in-law inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And your brother-in-law, as we saw from the photos today, was found with a wound to his stomach; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What kind of wound was it, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I saw this wound to his stomach. It was a horrible wound. I could no longer look at it. It was very big, and I just left immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking you to describe the wound. I'm sorry if I was unclear. I'm just wondering what was the cause of death to your brother-in-law, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This part here of his body was all damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you know, ma'am, though, was it inflicted by a gun-shot or a knife or some other manner?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you don't know his cause of death?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I don't, no. At that particular moment I was unable to tell what had caused his death. I was horrified.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Of course, ma'am. But did you subsequently at any time learn his cause of death?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No. All I know is that we found bullet casings and holes on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You didn't witness him being killed, did you, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you mentioned some other people today that were killed, an Astrit Rexha?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you didn't see him killed either, did you, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: About how old was he?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: About 30 something, 35 or 6. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you have any indication of when he was killed?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I don't have any indication when he was killed. When we came back to our home after the war, we were told that he was missing, that he could no longer be found alive. He was dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So it's assumed that he was killed because he's missing; correct, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: He was separated from the convoy. His mother explained to us how he was separated from the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Where was this, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: In Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: In Gjakove city or in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: In Gjakove city.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you mentioned another name, Agim Haxhi Avdylu, did you witness him being murdered?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Avdyli.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Avdyli, thank you, ma'am. Did you witness him being murdered?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't. His mother told me about this. His mother is actually my mother-in-law's sister.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: About how old was this man?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: About the same age as the other one.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And do they know that he was killed or is he also missing?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I don't know. She said that they had killed her son.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you don't know any of the specifies, do you, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And in your compound there were the three homes and you said that yours sustained fire damage. There was also fire damage to the summer home I believe it was?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But your brother-in-law's home was not damaged by fire?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And as we saw in that other photo, your neighbour's home wasn't damaged by fire?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, it wasn't either.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You didn't actually see how your house caught fire, did you, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I only saw the flames coming out from the windows and I saw the flames coming out of the roof.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And before you went on to gather your mother-in-law, you stated at one point while you were still in the stranger's yard, I believe, that: "... every now and then we would see young men - who we assumed were Kosovo Albanians - climbing over the perimeter walls of the garden running from yard to yard. Clearly these men were running from something or someone ..." And this is on page 4 of your statement. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, they were most probably running from the police. I didn't recognise their faces because this happened in the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you say "young men." How old do you mean when you say "young men"?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Twenty, 25, mostly 30, not older than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How were these young men dressed?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Normal clothes, everyday clothes, most frequently we wear track suits.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So they were in civilian clothing; yes, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, track suits, like young people wear.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were these possibly KLA members, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: There was no indication that they were members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What indication would you have expected to see if they were KLA members?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: A gesture of self-defence. They were just running for their lives. They were trying to escape.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Would you have expected a uniform, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you ever see KLA in Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Not in the part where I live. We didn't have any contacts with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was your brother-in-law a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I see you're shaking your head. I guess that's a no, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was your husband a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were any of your family members members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No one from my family was a member of the KLA. We were civilians, normal civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were you aware that Gjakove was a major KLA-held area during that time, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You weren't ever aware of their presence at all?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you never saw a KLA uniform in Gjakove, in the city?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, I wasn't interested in those things.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Is it possible because KLA members sometimes wore civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this may be a good time to take a break before I move into the last couple sections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I was a little surprised there could be more.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: We can continue on. I just wanted to -- the next one's a bit more lengthy. We can continue -- I'm happy to continue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That surprises me more, but we will give you the courtesy of a break now so that you can look at it. We will resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now for another break and resume at five to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Ms. Dula, I just have a few more questions relating to your leaving Gjakove. You say that after you felt unsafe at your own house you went to a shelter at the big temple; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Of course. You said that you felt unsafe at your house so you decided to shelter at the big temple; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And there were approximately a hundred people there you had stated; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And the police visited three times in those eight days you stated?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you're certain in your statement that they're police because -- and I quote: " ... they have the same blue camo uniform as that night ..." Correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How many of these people who you term as police came in a group to the big temple?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I could not see how many of them were, but the woman at whose house we were sheltering said that policemen had come and they were asking for things.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: This was the woman on the evening of the 24th and 25th?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, the woman of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, I'm actually referring to your statement when you talk about being at the big temple and you said that groups of police had visit -- would visit this temple. You said in your statement - this is on page 4: "They did not harm anybody but would demand things from the people they spoke to. They would ask for such things as car keys, money and ... items of value ..." So I'm wondering how many police came in a group to the big temple that you're describing here?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I already said earlier that I don't know how many of them were, but this woman came and said that they were asking for keys and valuables.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you never actually saw the police at the big temple; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, we were inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so it's only that you spoke to the woman who you had seen on the 25th and she said that this had happened; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The woman that lived in that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And then the following paragraph you state that: "On the eighth day we saw a crowd of many people walking past the temple, from the direction of the Qerim district of Gjakove. They were escorted by a mixture of VJ soldiers and Serbian police and, we assumed, were being led out of Gjakove. My family and I decided to join the crowd and having done so we were asked to hand in our identity documents to our escorts." Is this accurate? Other than there was the change of -- that you had now said it was just the police and not the VJ, is that correct, ma'am? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And mostly what I was getting at in this paragraph is that you say "I decided to join" -- "my family and I decided to join the crowd."

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So nobody forced you to join this crowd; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: We decided ourselves to join the crowd because we saw them walking by and we decided that we would go wherever the crowd would go.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And when you say "we," are you speaking of your husband, your children, and yourself or more of your extended family as well?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I include here my mother-in-law, the wife of my brother-in-law, and their children as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And when you joined into this group, did you approach the officers that asked for your identification to say that you wanted to join the group, or did they approach you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, we did not approach them and they did not approach us, did not say anything. We joined the crowd.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And it says: "... having done so we were asked to hand our identity documents to the escorts." Who were the escorts that you were asked to give your identity documents to?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Who told you to give the identity documents to the policemen?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They did. They asked for the identity documents at the first check-point. We had to leave there everything we had.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you weren't asked for your identity documents until you hit the first check-point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, at the first check-point and then additionally at the second check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And are you familiar with areas outside of Gjakove, ma'am, in Kosovo? Have you travelled much before this time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you know the route that you took to Qafa e Prushit?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But along the way you said that there were forces present. Can you describe what forces were there?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They were police forces initially, and then after some time we could see army.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And the two times that you were asked for your identification, how far out of Gjakove were you at the first check-point?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The first check-point is on the outskirts of Gjakove where the town boundary is.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And that's where you had told the police asking for them that they were burned in your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did any of you have any identity documents with you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you had left yours in your home when you fled the night before and it burnt there; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It wasn't possible for us to take anything. We just wanted to get away and survive.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Where were the identity documents of your mother-in-law, sister-in-law, and the children?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I don't know, but they didn't have them on them either.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And you say: "Interestingly the police responded by saying that NATO had in fact burnt them up ..." Ma'am, do you think that's possibly because the NATO air-strikes had started the fire and that's what they meant by that?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How far were you out of Gjakove at the second check-point?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The second check-point was located before the part where you get to the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you stated today it was by barracks. What barracks are these?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: That was a kind of a structure with a roof. It was an isolated structure.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But how did you know it was barracks, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I could hear people that -- We are here at the sentry box. The people that we were together with, that's what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this was just before you reached Albania; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Can you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were these barracks at this second check-point, that's just before you reached Albania; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but we had to walk a long way before we got to the territory of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you said at about this point you saw some damaging of window-panes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Of the shops. Are you asking me about the shops?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you don't know what town or village that was in, do you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: This was on the way from the house we were sheltering in onwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When exactly did you see these windows being damaged? What date approximately?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: On the same day we left together with the crowd.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And the people you saw doing this, they were wearing what?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: They were wearing police uniforms, the ones that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So, again, blue camouflage; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I didn't dare look around very much. I just glanced for a little bit. I just looked for a little bit and then straight ahead. I couldn't look around very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And how many people did you see doing this?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: There were groups of them. I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And all of them were wearing camouflage, the same colour you saw that evening in your yard?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And the two times you were asked for identification, again by people in blue camouflage; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did they have any other insignia or indication of -- that they were police?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I couldn't tell whether there were any insignia. I just remember the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you know where they were police from?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: How could I know?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did they ever say why they were asking for your identification?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, they didn't. They just collected them and put them in a box.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you ever give a statement to anyone other than the ICTY, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. O'Leary. Ms. Gopalan, you will need to finish by 1.45. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Dula, I have a few questions for you arising from Defence counsel's questions during cross-examination. During cross-examination you were asked about the people who came to your home and expelled you, you and your family, on the night of the 24th and 25th of March. This is in page 45, line 7. You were asked about who they were and you said that you can understand who they are because of their accent and that when they spoke you can see who they are. Could you tell us from the accent that you heard when they spoke, what conclusion did you form as to who they were?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: In my opinion, they were all policemen from Gjakove, from their accent.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What is it that you heard in their accent that indicated to you that they were from Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: In Gjakove the Serbs living there had a different accent from the other people elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to clarify, what language is it that you heard the Serbs speaking?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, moving on to your journey back to your home on the morning of the 25th of March, you were asked whether you returned directly to your family compound and you said: "No, I did not go directly," because you were trying to see if there was anybody around, "whether I was in any danger." This is in page 55, line 9. Could you tell us what sort of danger you were fearing on that morning.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I feared for my life. I feared that I would be killed by someone.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did you have any idea as to who would be -- who could have killed you on that day?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I thought that the people who entered our yard would be around there and they could kill me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You were also asked some questions about your brother-in-law and his family - this is at page 61, line 1 - and you say that when you returned on the morning of the 25th you saw your brother-in-law's family with a neighbour where they had taken shelter. And you learned that that family had been made to leave the house the night before and they had detained your brother-in-law inside the house. Could you tell us who you mean when you say "they detained my brother-in-law inside the house," if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The policemen who entered.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how did you learn this?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The policemen who attacked us that night were the same ones who entered that part where my brother-in-law's house was.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And did you learn why it is your brother-in-law was detained, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, moving on to some questions you were asked about Astrit Rexha, you explained that his mother had told you that he was separated from a convoy. Now, this is page 62, line 24. Did you also learn from his mother who had separated him from the convoy?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Are you able to offer an approximation as to when this occurred, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did his mother indicate to you when it was he was separated from the convoy approximately, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No, she didn't mention the date to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did she provide a time-period, even if she didn't specify the date?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: That month when we were expelled from our town, within this time-period.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Dula. Now, you were also asked some questions about the NATO attack in Djakovica - this is in page 37, line 1 - and you said that the attack started at around 8.00 p.m. on the 24th of March. And you agreed with Defence counsel that on that night from around 8.00 you and your family went inside your house and nobody left. Just to clarify, is it correct that in response to the NATO attack that took place around the -- around 8.00 p.m. on the 24th of March, your family returned to your home, you went inside your home and stayed inside?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No. At that time we were not afraid of NATO.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that you were not afraid of NATO, and therefore what happened at around 8.00 when the NATO attack started happening? What did you and your family do in response?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: We stayed inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And when is it you left your home at that time? What happened that made you subsequently leave your home?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: The attack by the police, the attack from the ground, the police that entered our courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Dula. Now, you were also asked some questions about the window-panes that you saw damaged. You say they were damaged by men wearing police uniform and that you didn't dare look much. This was in page 71, line 16. I'd like to know where it is you saw these men damaging the window-panes, in which town, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: In Gjakove when we joined the convoy and as we were walking along with the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Dula. You were also asked some questions by Defence counsel about the buildings in your family compound. You were asked about the home of your brother-in-law. If I could just take you to the section. You say: "A. The old house was a historical building. It was a 200-years'-old house." "Q. Which house was that, ma'am? "A. The one where my brother-in-law" --

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I'm talking here about my brother-in-law's house, the house where he lived. This is the house that was about 200 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Dula. Now, did any other buildings, any of the other houses in your family compound, also have historical significance, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And could you tell us what was the condition of this 200-year-old house when you went back to the family compound on the next day?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE DULA
utterances.text: I simply couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the damage inside. There were bullet-holes all over the walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Dula.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do not have any further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mrs. Dula, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber is grateful that you've been able to come to The Hague and to assist us and for the statement which we've now received and which we'll be able to consider in due course. We thank you for that. You may, of course, now return to your normal life and activities, and the Court Officer will assist you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next witness, as we indicated via e-mail, is K20, who should be available to testify tomorrow provided that her health situation is stable. In the meantime, in the remainder of the session, Ms. Kravetz has a procedural application to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's a very neat way of passing the baton. Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I hope it will only take a couple of minutes. It's a procedural matter that concerns the testimony of Mr. Byrnes of last Friday. We would like to make an oral application to change the status of his -- of a portion of his testimony of last Friday from confidential to public and this is a portion at pages 8228 to 8229. As Your Honours probably remember, we heard that portion of the evidence in private session in order to protect material that is subject to Rule 70 restrictions. The Rule 70 provider has since reviewed the entire transcript and has agreed to release that portion of the transcript to the public. So at this stage we would apply for an order of the Trial Chamber to modify the status from a confidential/private to open/public session. That's all, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this the whole of pages 8228 and 8229?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I believe the private session starts somewhere at the top of 8228 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's the whole of that section?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There would seem to be no reason for resisting that motion; it will be granted. We therefore should adjourn now to resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
